summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with diffuse abdominal and back pain, mild shortness of breath, and suspected fever. She had recently been hospitalized for decompensated diastolic heart failure and was not taking her furosemide at home. On admission, she had signs of urinary tract infection with a positive urinalysis, and was started on IV antibiotics, later narrowed to oral Bactrim. Pulmonary edema was confirmed on imaging, and she was treated with IV furosemide before transitioning to oral therapy. Her Foley catheter was changed to reduce infection risk. A CT scan showed no acute abdominal process but confirmed cirrhotic liver changes. Lower extremity ultrasound ruled out DVT. She improved clinically and was discharged on oral furosemide and a 7-day course of Bactrim, with instructions to monitor daily weight and follow up with her providers.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Asymptomatic human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] infection status
Unspecified viral hepatitis B without hepatic coma
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
